corpus_attestation.note: Each arm is attested from its OWN Slurm log glob and validated against its OWN study root, so an attestation can never cross the join. Absence of a log means UNATTESTED, not v1: results.json records no corpus path, and key_list_sha256 cannot discriminate the corpora (identical ISO text). The corpus= token is a LABEL derived by the launcher from the resolved data dirs; the dirs and data_source are the evidence, and single_corpus catches only mixtures, never a uniformly wrong corpus.

1042.note: Absence of a log means UNATTESTED, not v1. results.json records no corpus path, so an unattested cell's corpus is established only from its W&B config / Hydra snapshot. Attestation matches a log to a cell by run name, which the _smoke study root reuses verbatim — study_root_mismatches lists any matched log whose own output_dir echo belongs to a different study root. The corpus= token is a LABEL, not evidence (RV_DATA_DIR/MS_DATA_DIR are launcher overrides): corpus_mismatches lists every attested cell whose echoed data dirs or data_source do not establish the expected v2 corpus, which is what single_corpus cannot catch — it sees mixtures, not a uniformly wrong corpus.

curve_deltas.selection_note: 4 points admit 6 ordered pairs; this bundle publishes 4 — the 3 consecutive steps plus the endpoint (1042→10420) — and omits 1042→5210, 2605→10420. Publishing all of them at n=3 would multiply the family for no new information: every contrast here is a WITHIN-SEED difference of the same seed's values, so each omitted pair is the exact per-seed sum of published consecutive steps (e.g. 1042→5210 = [1042→2605] + [2605→5210], seed by seed) and is reconstructible by adding two per_seed_diff columns of tables/curve_deltas.csv. The published set is therefore minimal and complete: the steps carry the shape question, the endpoint carries the headline, and nothing that was measured is hidden.

grid_integrity.note: The dir name and results.json are two independent records of a cell's seed and must agree. A point whose present cells do not carry distinct seeds is not an n-seed point no matter what n the table prints.

maingrid_consistency.note: The inherited 100% point is another study's published result, so it is checked against that study's committed aggregate.json rather than trusted because a path was passed. Both sides are agg.summarize over the same results.json floats, so the tolerance covers JSON round-tripping only.

minimum_target_ratio_note: Not emitted. The v1 study adequacy rule scans the five mix ratios for the smallest target-notation training share whose mean target-view CER clears a pre-registered threshold. Over three ratios the scan has a different resolution, so running it here would silently redefine a pre-registered rule on a coarser grid rather than reproduce it. PENDING(v2-data-efficiency-study) keeps that table open.
retention_adaptation_note: Not emitted. agg.retention_adaptation contrasts a single-notation baseline against a 25% minority mix, i.e. rv_ratio 0.75 and 0.25. This study trains only {1.0, 0.5, 0.0}, so the contrast has NO counterpart at ANY trained total ([1042, 2605, 5210]) and cannot be a curve. Emitting it as an empty or 10420-only table would read as 'measured, no effect'. The 10420 retention/adaptation contrasts are in the v2 main-grid bundle, where all five ratios exist.

shape.claim_note: The four points do NOT determine a curve shape. 'Front-loaded', 'log-linear', 'saturates by X%' and 'the gain is concentrated in the first step' are all claims about how the step magnitudes compare, and comparing them needs the steps to be separable from each other, which n=3 cannot deliver (separability_note). What the curve does establish is each point's own mean with an interval, and each step's paired difference with an interval and a sign-consistency flag. Step rankings in this bundle are printed only next to the separability table and are ordered DESCRIPTIONS of three seeds, never findings. The interior points still earn their cost: they replace an unmeasured interval between 10% and 100% with measured intermediate levels, which is what rules out 'the curve was never looked at between the endpoints' — a weaker and honest statement than a shape.
shape.separability_note: No step and no pair of steps is statistically separable at n=3. The exact paired sign-flip permutation test's smallest attainable two-sided p is 2/2**3 = 0.25, so neither 'this step is a real gain' nor 'this step is larger than that one' can be established in either direction. A step is classified only as consistently signed across the three seeds, and a pair of steps only as consistently ordered across them (a description of those seeds) or unstable. Source of the floor: paclic-v2-effect-sizes-and-plateau (SEPARABILITY_NOTE), which reaches the same ceiling on the ratio plateau.

join_wide.scope: every present cell of EVERY total; total_train_samples_requested and parallel_keys_used are excluded on purpose — they are the curve's axis

subset_consistency.key_list_sha256_note: key_list_sha256 hashes the ordered shared-parallel ISO *text* keys. The v2 corpus re-renders the SAME text, so this hash is identical between v1 and v2 by construction and CANNOT attest which image corpus a cell consumed. Use corpus_attestation (Slurm .out header) for that.
subset_consistency.key_list_sha256_scope_note: key_list_sha256 hashes the ORDERED selected key list. dataset.py sorts the shared keys, applies a seeded shuffle (parallel_subset_seed is left null, so it follows `seed`) and takes a PREFIX of length total_train_samples. So within one (seed, total) all 3 ratios share one list — rv_ratio only reroutes an already-selected text to an RV or an MS image — while the same seed at a different total is a different ordered list with a different hash. The invariant is therefore WITHIN (seed, total), one step weaker than the main grid's within-seed one, and a healthy join carries exactly 12 distinct hashes (3 seeds x 4 totals). Checking it join-wide, or even per seed, makes a healthy curve report 'this is not a single study'.

nesting.note: The launcher leaves parallel_subset_seed null (unlike the v1 study study, which pinned 42) so every point's interval means 'all variation downstream of `seed`'. Nesting is not sacrificed by that: dataset.py sorts the shared keys, shuffles them with a seed that does NOT depend on total_train_samples, and takes a prefix, so within one seed 1042 ⊂ 2605 ⊂ 5210 ⊂ 10420 holds by construction, and at 10420 the selected key SET is the whole shared-parallel corpus anyway. Because that is what makes a consecutive step mean 'the same lines plus these', it is CHECKED against each cell's committed parallel_keys.txt (subset_nesting) rather than trusted. What the unpinned seed buys is that a low-data interval also covers subset-sampling variation, which is the honest interval for 'only n lines were available'; the cost is that two points' error bars are not subset-matched ACROSS seeds, so a paired delta is a delta between two conditions, not between two runs on one subset.
nesting.scope: within each seed, every consecutive pair of totals on the curve's x axis
